components.name: Primary Button
components.description: The single strong action in a working context.
components.css: .ds-button-primary { min-height: 40px; padding: 0 15px; border: 1px solid #c9471b; border-radius: 9px; background: #c9471b; color: #fff; font: 680 15px/1.5 Inter, ui-sans-serif, sans-serif; cursor: pointer; } .ds-button-primary:hover { border-color: #a83a16; background: #a83a16; } .ds-button-primary:focus-visible { outline: 3px solid #b43f17; outline-offset: 2px; }

components.name: Text Field
components.css: .ds-field { display: grid; gap: 6px; color: #172033; font: 680 13px/1.5 Inter, ui-sans-serif, sans-serif; } .ds-field input { min-height: 42px; padding: 9px 11px; border: 1px solid #c4ccd7; border-radius: 9px; background: #fff; color: #172033; font-weight: 400; } .ds-field input:focus-visible { outline: 3px solid #b43f17; outline-offset: 2px; }

components.name: Status Badge
components.description: Compact positive state used inside dense data views.
components.css: .ds-badge { display: inline-flex; align-items: center; min-height: 24px; padding: 2px 8px; border-radius: 999px; background: #edf7f3; color: #17765a; font: 700 12px/1.5 Inter, ui-sans-serif, sans-serif; }

components.name: Data Surface
components.description: The flat bordered perimeter shared by tables and master-detail views.
components.css: .ds-data-surface { display: grid; gap: 4px; padding: 16px; border: 1px solid #dce1e8; border-radius: 12px; background: #fff; color: #172033; font: 400 15px/1.5 Inter, ui-sans-serif, sans-serif; } .ds-data-surface strong { font-weight: 700; } .ds-data-surface span { color: #5c667a; font-size: 13px; } .ds-data-surface:hover { background: #fcfcfd; }

components.name: Active Navigation Item
components.description: A compact dark-rail destination with an orange active signal.
components.css: .ds-nav-item { display: flex; align-items: center; gap: 11px; min-height: 42px; padding: 0 11px; border-radius: 9px; background: #2a364b; color: #fff; font: 600 15px/1.5 Inter, ui-sans-serif, sans-serif; text-decoration: none; } .ds-nav-item > span:first-child { color: #ff8a5d; } .ds-nav-item:hover { background: #344158; } .ds-nav-item:focus-visible { outline: 3px solid #b43f17; outline-offset: 2px; }

narrative.overview:
Otakuma Auth is a compact operations console: dependable, direct, and quiet enough to keep attention on identity data. Auth0 supplies the familiar management grammar while Cloudflare supplies the dense, infrastructure-oriented workbench. Brand appears through ink navy, paper-white working surfaces, and a rare warm-orange signal.

The system avoids a generic dashboard of decorative metric cards. APIs and their Applications are the organizing relationship, with lists and details kept close enough to support fast operational comparison.

Authentication uses the same visual world at a more declarative scale: a dark identity field holds product and security context while a white credential sheet keeps the one-way bootstrap or sign-in task focused.

rules.name: The Signal Rule
rules.body: Orange marks an action or selected object; it is never used as broad decoration.

dos: Do preserve the API-to-Applications relationship as the primary information architecture.
Do keep destructive consequences beside their action and require confirmation.
Do use native controls and clear focus states for keyboard operation.
donts: Don't call an OAuth Application a “client” in product copy.
Don't turn orange into decorative surface area or add vanity metric cards.
Don't persist, log, or redisplay an Application credential.
Don't hide operational data behind hover-only interactions.
